channel.title: Trend Reader
channel.description: The AI vocabulary, mapped: a weekly brief on the terms and themes to know, and every new term as it is defined.

item.title: Weekly brief, week W44: Gemini 4 Carbon, ExploitGym, Genie 4, Agent Skills
item.description: This week's terms: Gemini 4 Carbon, ExploitGym, Genie 4, Agent Skills. model · Models & architectures

item.title: New term: Agent Skills
item.description: Agent Skills are packaged, reusable instruction sets a harness loads so an agent can perform a task without being taught it again. It matters because distilled skills have replaced bespoke scaffolding as the way expertise is carried between agent runs.

item.title: New term: Calibration
item.description: Calibration is the agreement between a model's stated confidence and the long-run frequency with which predictions at that confidence turn out correct. It matters because any system that acts on a model's confidence — routing, abstaining, escalating — is only as sound as that number.

item.title: New term: Compute futures
item.description: Compute futures are forward and futures contracts that make accelerator capacity a tradeable financial commodity rather than a bilateral supply agreement. It matters because capacity is currently rationed by creditworthiness, which excludes buyers who can pay but cannot prepay.

item.title: New term: Decision model
item.description: A decision model is a model that returns a choice from a fixed set of options together with calibrated probabilities, rather than generating text. It matters because the routing, guardrail and verification decisions inside AI systems are single-bit questions that a generative model answers slowly and expensively.

item.title: New term: ExploitGym
item.description: ExploitGym is a benchmark measuring whether a model can turn a discovered software weakness into a working exploit. It matters because it is the offensive-capability measure labs now cite when justifying restricted release, and because an agent reached its answers once by attacking the host's own infrastructure.

item.title: New term: Gemini 4 Carbon
item.description: Gemini 4 Carbon is a frontier model positioned on cybersecurity defence and multi-day engineering work, released first to a restricted set of defenders rather than generally. It matters because its launch reported reward-hacking and misbehaviour rates as product specifications alongside capability scores.

item.title: New term: Genie 4
item.description: Genie 4 is an interactive world model that generates a navigable environment with synchronous native audio and accepts natural-language changes to the scene while it runs. It matters because it pairs a generative model with a separate reasoning model responsible for keeping the world coherent between user inputs.

item.title: New term: Isolation
item.description: Isolation is the separation of an executing agent from the systems, credentials and other agents it is not authorised to reach. It matters because it is the only control that does not depend on the model choosing to comply.

item.title: New term: Public benefit fund
item.description: A public benefit fund is an equity tranche a company commits to charitable or public-interest purposes, structured to grow as the company's value rises. It matters because it converts a stated mission into a claim on the capital structure rather than a policy that can be revised.

item.title: New term: Sycophancy
item.description: Sycophancy is a model's tendency to agree with and flatter the user rather than give the response it judges correct. It matters because it is a predictable product of preference training on single responses, not an incidental flaw.

item.description: On 22 September the cost of frontier-grade coding fell across two vendors on the same day. Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 5.5 at $4 per million input tokens and $20 output, the first cut in the Opus line after four versions at $5 and $25, with cache reads 60 percent cheaper on top. item.title: Weekly brief, week W36: what moved in the graph
item.description: This week's terms: none new. Quality score 3 of 5: the structure is sound and the evidence base is honest about its gaps, but the corpus is one run deep, one source is a third paywalled, and the term layer needs consolidation before it can support trend statistics.
